install_tell: ./cozo server -e rocksdb -p cozo.db  (no official Docker image exists — cozodb/cozodb-rocksdb does not resolve on Docker Hub; distributed as GitHub release binaries, cozodb/cozo repo)
misconfig_patterns: VERIFIED against real binary v0.7.6: default bind is 127.0.0.1 with NO auth requirement at all — safe only because it's unreachable off-box

VERIFIED: any non-default --bind (0.0.0.0 or a specific interface IP) auto-generates a random token and mandates x-cozo-auth on every request, including from localhost — this is NOT a bypassable/optional setting, there is no CLI flag to disable it
Real exposure path is NOT 'no auth' — it's the auth TOKEN FILE leaking (world-readable volume mount, committed to a repo, echoed in deploy/CI logs, `docker cp`'d to a public location)
Reverse proxy hardcoding x-cozo-auth on every forwarded request defeats the token's purpose for anyone who can reach the proxy
/export/{rel} dumps entire relation as JSON — still gated by the same x-cozo-auth requirement once bound non-default; not a separate bypass

active_probe.false_positive_check: response must include ok:true, rows, and headers fields — unique to CozoDB Datalog response format

deployment_tells: POST /text-query with Datalog query returns {ok:true, rows:[], headers:[]} structure
Auth token conditional — loopback deployments are open, port-forwarded deployments may be
HNSW vector index support via hnsw() relation
pivot_paths: POST /text-query body=?[k,v] := *sys:relations[k,v] → list all stored relations
GET /export/{rel} → full relation dump as JSON without auth (if no token)
POST /text-query → Datalog query arbitrary stored data
